# Runbook — the dead-man's switch (Successor-Remediation, Op Stds §43)

>   - The daemon plane — liveness, breaker, alerts, row-cap, picklists, guards → Heartbeats + watchdog Check C keep daemons honest → “Healthchecks.io emails you that ITS has stopped checking in.”

A §43 successor-remediation entry, written for the **Successor-Operator**: a
trained operator who runs Claude Code and reads Smartsheet rows + alert emails,
but does **not** read code or touch secrets. The §42 code-reader rationale lives
in `shared/heartbeat_client.py` and `scripts/watchdog.py::_check_heartbeat_armed`.

## Purpose

What to do when the watchdog reports **"DEAD-MAN'S SWITCH DISARMED"** (Check Z),
or when the outside monitor emails you that ITS has **stopped checking in**.

These are two different alarms pointing in opposite directions, and telling them
apart is the whole job of this page:

| You saw | Meaning | Go to |
|---|---|---|
| An ITS CRITICAL saying **DEAD-MAN'S SWITCH DISARMED** | ITS is alive. Its ability to report its own death is broken. | [Symptom 1](#symptom-1--dead-mans-switch-disarmed) |
| An email **from Healthchecks.io** saying a check is DOWN | ITS stopped checking in. The Mac may be dead. | [Symptom 2](#symptom-2--healthchecksio-says-its-is-down) |
| Neither, and ITS has simply gone quiet | See [Symptom 3](#symptom-3--its-is-quiet-and-nothing-alerted) — this is the failure this whole mechanism exists to prevent. | [Symptom 3](#symptom-3--its-is-quiet-and-nothing-alerted) |

## What the heartbeat is, in one paragraph

Every hour the watchdog finishes its checks and makes a single web request to a
private URL at Healthchecks.io. Healthchecks.io does not care what the request
says — it only notes the time. If it stops hearing from ITS for longer than the
period you configured, it emails you.

That inversion is the point. **Every other ITS alarm needs ITS to be running in
order to fire.** If the Mac loses power, fills its disk, gets logged out, or has
its background jobs unloaded, all the ordinary alarms go silent together —
silence is exactly what a healthy quiet night looks like too. The heartbeat is
the only signal where the *absence* of the message is itself the message.

The URL lives in one place: the `ITS_Config` row **`system.heartbeat_url`**
(Workstream `global`). If that cell is empty, or still holds the seeded
`PLACEHOLDER_…` text, or is not an `https://` address, the watchdog **skips the
ping entirely and says nothing louder than an INFO log line.** That is why
Check Z exists: to make the skip loud.

## Symptom 1 — "DEAD-MAN'S SWITCH DISARMED"

**What you'll see.** A CRITICAL from `scripts.watchdog` whose message begins
`DEAD-MAN'S SWITCH DISARMED`. It names which of the three cases applies:
still the seed placeholder, blank, or not an https URL.

**What it means.** ITS is fine right now — this alarm proves ITS is running well
enough to complain. What is broken is its ability to tell you if it dies later.
Treat it as urgent but not an outage.

**Repair (Tier-2, low-capability-class).**

1. Open the operator dashboard → **Config** (or the `ITS_Config` sheet directly).
2. Find the row **`system.heartbeat_url`**, Workstream **`global`**.
3. Compare the **Value** against the ping URL for the ITS check in the
   Healthchecks.io account. It looks like
   `https://hc-ping.com/` followed by a long dash-separated code.
4. If the Value is wrong, blank, or still says `PLACEHOLDER_…`, paste the
   correct ping URL in and save.
5. Wait for the next watchdog run (hourly). Check Z should report
   `heartbeat beacon armed`.
6. Confirm from the other side: in Healthchecks.io the ITS check should move to
   green and show a "last ping" time within the last hour.

**Do NOT** paste anything other than the ping URL for the ITS check. A URL from
some other check silences the real alarm while looking healthy — the worst of
both states.

**Escalate to Seth if:** you cannot find the Healthchecks.io ping URL, the
account is inaccessible, or step 5 does not clear after two watchdog runs.
Anything requiring a new monitor to be provisioned is Seth's — it needs an
account credential, which is a FIXED high-capability class (secrets/auth).

## Symptom 2 — Healthchecks.io says ITS is DOWN

**What you'll see.** An email from Healthchecks.io (not from ITS) saying the ITS
check is DOWN or has not reported in.

**What it means.** ITS stopped pinging. Either the Mac is off/asleep/crashed, it
lost internet, or the watchdog job stopped running. **You will usually get no
ITS alert at all alongside this** — that is expected, and it is precisely why
this monitor exists.

**Repair (Tier-2, low-capability-class).**

1. **Is the Mac on and awake?** Power, network, and logged in. Most DOWN alerts
   end here. Waking it is often the entire fix.
2. **Is it reachable?** If you can reach it remotely (Tailscale), do so.
3. **Did ITS come back on its own?** Once the Mac is awake, wait for the next
   hourly watchdog run and check Healthchecks.io for a fresh ping. Background
   jobs restart themselves on their own schedule; a Mac that was merely asleep
   generally needs nothing else.
4. **Still down after the next hour?** Check whether the ITS background jobs are
   loaded — the dashboard's daemons panel is the quickest read if you can reach
   it.
5. **Check for a knock-on backlog.** After a long outage, look at
   `ITS_Review_Queue` and any pending-review sheets — work that arrived while
   ITS was down is waiting, not lost.

**A false alarm is possible and is not a defect.** A Mac closed overnight, an
internet outage, or a maintenance window can all trip a DOWN email while nothing
is actually broken. Confirm liveness first; do not start repairing.

**Escalate to Seth if:** the Mac is on, awake, online, and still not pinging
after two hours; or the background jobs are not loaded and you do not have a
documented step that reloads them.

## Symptom 3 — ITS is quiet and nothing alerted

If ITS has produced no output for a while and **neither** alarm above fired,
suspect the beacon itself:

1. Check Healthchecks.io directly. Is the ITS check green, and how old is the
   last ping?
2. Check the `system.heartbeat_url` row as in Symptom 1.
3. Check whether Healthchecks.io alert emails are going to a mailbox someone
   actually reads.

Between 2026-05-28 and 2026-08-17 this exact combination was live: the row held
its placeholder, so no ping was ever sent, so the monitor never had anything to
miss. Nothing was broken loudly; the detector simply was not switched on.

## What this does NOT cover

Check Z proves the URL is **configured**. It does not prove Healthchecks.io has
**received** a recent ping — reading that back needs a Healthchecks management
API key, which ITS does not hold. The residual gap is narrow: a configured URL
plus a running watchdog produces a ping, and if the watchdog is not running,
that is the condition Healthchecks.io detects by itself. Tracked in
`docs/tech_debt.md`.

## Escalation boundary (observable terms)

| Situation | Who |
|---|---|
| The `system.heartbeat_url` Value is wrong and you have the correct ping URL | **You** — one cell edit |
| Healthchecks.io DOWN email, Mac was asleep/offline, it recovers | **You** |
| A new Healthchecks.io check must be created, or the account is inaccessible | **Seth** — credential/account act |
| Mac is on, online, and still not pinging after two hours | **Seth** |
| The alarm keeps firing after a correct URL is set | **Seth** — code-level |

Anything touching a credential, or any change to code, is a FIXED
high-capability class and escalates regardless of how well documented it is.
